claims.text: Lint and compile: project code (src, tests, evals) is ruff-clean and compiles. The only ruff findings in the worktree are helper scripts under .bridgie/runs/ from earlier seats, which are outside the package.
claims.proof_cmd: ruff check src tests evals && python -m compileall -q src tests
claims.proof_output: All checks passed!  (compileall: no output, exit 0)

claims.text: Full suite passes with the hardening test added.

claims.proof_output: invariants: 101 passed; contracts: 65 passed; dual_run: 83 passed

claims.text: Each of the four verify-27 findings is a test with the R4 outcome: HMRC plus savings move wording, and a refund plus savings-transfer wording, are ambiguous with both candidates recorded. Counter cash at a GRANT branch is ambiguous, not trading. A bare TAX POT label is not own-account. End to end under cma run, they are outside M2 and inside M16's evidence.

Determinism (design Rollout): shuffling the lists within each stage under 8 seeds gives the same verdict on every credit sample. A pairwise matrix of more than 1000 pairs shows that no exception in one list hides another list's wording.

No hidden tie-break: credit_verdict treats a cue whose pattern is anchored with ^ as the bank's code. A new contract test pins returned_dd as the only anchored, categorised cue. It also shows that UNPAID DD written later in payer text does not settle the line.
Idempotency: categorising the same statement twice under v2, with an override, a profile and a firm rule, gives the same category, rule id and reversal link on every line.
Rollback: CMA_RULESET=v1 on a statement already categorised under v2 gives exactly the categories and rule ids of a fresh v1 run, with no data repair. The offline evals pass under both tables.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q -m dual_run; CMA_RULESET=v1|v2 python evals/run_evals.py --llm fake --out <tmp>
claims.proof_output: dual_run: 83 passed; '9/9 memos fully grounded; model = fake; ruleset = v2'; '9/9 memos fully grounded; model = fake; ruleset = v1'

claims.text: Migration and consumers: the evidence 'lines' key is additive and holds ids only, with no descriptions. Legacy checkpoints from before T01 and from T02 replay v1 rule ids, and a stale hash replays nothing. v1 stays frozen and pinned. P7 lists every committed line v2 changes.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q -m 'contracts or dual_run or invariants'
claims.proof_output: test_evidence_lines_carry_ids_only_never_descriptions, test_a_t02_checkpoint_..._replays_v1, test_p7_v2_changes_only_the_listed_lines_and_m1_m16_only_where_listed: passed within the tiers above

claims.text: Authz and security: no new entry point. The only control is the existing CMA_RULESET env var, which refuses an unknown id. Payer text is matched only, never interpolated, and is kept out of evidence. Rule tables are validated on load, including patterns that fail to compile. No new dependency, no secrets.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rules_v2.py -k 'malformed or keep_its_stages or descriptions'

claims.text: Performance: categorising 10,000 lines under v2 with a profile stays under the design's 2 s recompute budget.
Observability: every line's provenance, including the v2:conflict:<a>+<b> form, is written to the evidence file by cma run. The eval summary names the ruleset it ran with.

Docs: the README categoriser row now gives revision 3's precedence, including the ambiguous verdict, its v2:conflict: provenance, and that it is never trading receipts. The categorise.py and v2.yaml headers already describe the verdict.

notes: Gaps for the owner, none of them in T03's scope: (1) Own-account pairing (R8) as a precedence-(3) settler of an ambiguous credit is Tier 2 and not wired; classify takes a profile and overrides, but no CLI command supplies them yet (case store, C3). (2) Firm rules are accepted by classify and are not loaded by cma run (R20/R21 are Tier 2). (3) The ambiguous-credit count and candidate pairs in cma report (Observability, R50/C11) and the judgement-queue display (C5) are later tasks; today the signal exists only as rule_id in the evidence lines. No remote alert, by design. (4) Which reading of D52 the owner meant (agreeing cues outrank names) is still an open design question; the code follows design rev 3. (5) The bank-code detection relies on a '^' anchor convention; it is now pinned by a test rather than by a schema field. Making it a schema flag would change the table format, so I left it to the owner. (6) No changelog file exists in the repo; the README is the release note. (7) Working-tree ruff findings are only in .bridgie/runs/*/ helper scripts left by earlier seats. Changes are left uncommitted for the orchestrator.
